conviction_note: Sum of a +3.0 operating datapoint (a prospectus-only May-31 backlog print that implies Q4 bookings running ~15% above the record quarter every preview anchors on), +1.5 for a guided capex cliff that lands in the FY27 outlook nobody's dilution narrative mentions, and -1.5 for the reflexive Neos supply that punishes exactly the upside the -22.5 vol-point skew is paying for; well inside the 16.23% implied move because this is the most heavily covered name in the window.

findings.finding: Forgent's 1 July 2026 424B4 discloses backlog rose ~20% from ~$2.0bn at 31 Mar 2026 to ~$2.4bn at 31 May 2026 - a two-month, ~$400m build that, netted against the ~$261-288m of revenue implied by the company's own $392-432m Q4 guide over those two months, means April+May bookings alone ran ~$660-690m (~$330-345m/month) versus the record Q3 pace of $867m/quarter ($289m/month), with June still to come.
findings.why_not_priced: Interim backlog disclosed inside a follow-on prospectus never enters a consensus field, a Zacks/StockTitan preview, or an aggregator page. Every piece of preview and wire copy on this print still anchors on '$1.98bn backlog, $867m bookings' from the 14 May release - the sweep's own already_in_the_wire list does exactly that. If the tape held the $2.4bn number and the ~$330m/month bookings run-rate it implies, the FY27 guide would be treated as largely pre-funded by backlog and the stock would not be making a 52-week low the session before the print at 0.59x the $49.00 July deal price; the coverage would be arguing about backlog conversion, not about Neos supply.
findings.independence: StockTitan's separate summary of the same 424B4 carries the identical $2.0bn-to-$2.4bn line (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/FPS/424b4-forgent-power-solutions-inc-prospectus-filed-pursuant-to-rule-4-3d17361d33c7.html) - SAME DOCUMENT, so treat it as one source cluster, not corroboration. Genuinely independent support for the demand direction is thin: industry lead-time surveys still show MV switchgear at 52-80 weeks and substation transformers at 75-110 weeks in 2026 (https://terrapincg.com/news/switchgear-transformer-generator-lead-times-2026), which is consistent but not company-specific.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call the CFO guided capex down to ~1-1.5% of revenue 'going forward' from the $205m five-plant expansion program, with the expansion 'substantially completed by the end of fiscal 2026' and the resulting footprint able to support up to $5bn of annual revenue - so the FY2027 outlook management pre-committed to give on this specific call ('we will provide our outlook for fiscal 2027' on the fiscal Q4 call) is the first one that carries a real free-cash-flow line.
findings.why_not_priced: Every piece of published explanation for the 55% drawdown is about share supply and dilution - the Motley Fool's 21 Aug piece names only the Neos sell-down and the 4 Aug lockup, and the tickeron/press coverage of the July deal names only dilution. None of it mentions capital intensity falling from roughly 15% of revenue to 1-1.5%. If the FCF inflection were in the price, the bear case in print would be about backlog conversion or margin, not about who is selling stock; and a company about to print its first self-funding year would not be trading below the price of its own 30 March follow-on ($29.50).
findings.independence: The Q3 earnings release itself (different URL, same 14 May event) states capex 'related almost entirely to the Company's capacity expansion plan, which remains on track to be substantially completed by the end of fiscal 2026' - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2080126/000208012626000017/exhibit991earningsrelease_.htm . Same-day cluster with the transcript; count once.

findings.finding: Neos Partners has sold down through three registered deals in five months at progressively whatever price the tape offered - 30 Mar at $29.50, 1 Jun at $47.00, and 1 Jul at $49.00 including 29,094,075 selling-stockholder shares - taking voting power from ~81% post-IPO to below 50%, and the July prospectus still shows continuing equity owners at 51.54% of Opco economics, so a fourth S-1 is the standard response to any post-print strength.
findings.why_not_priced: The overhang is written about, but the positioning says the reflexivity is not: the baseline's 25-delta skew is -22.46 vol points with a put/call open-interest ratio of 0.30, i.e. the options market is paying up for upside on a name whose last three up-moves were each terminated by a marketed offering. If the 'a rally is the trigger for deal four' mechanic were priced, upside calls would not be the bid side of a 178% IV chain and the skew would be flat or positive. Note this finding shares the 424B4 with finding 1 and reads the opposite side of it - the deal document is both the source of the backlog datapoint and the evidence of the supply.
findings.independence: Separately sourced: The Motley Fool, 21 Aug 2026, attributes the slump to Neos 'selling its stake through multiple stock offerings since the IPO' plus the 4 Aug lockup expiry - https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/21/why-forgent-power-stock-slumped-this-week-and-what/ . Different author, different document.

searched_and_found_nothing: Securities class action or SEC/law-firm investigation following the 55% post-IPO drawdown - nothing filed against Forgent that I could find (search returned only Power Solutions International, PSIX, a different company)

Glassdoor/Indeed employee reviews or layoff chatter at the Dayton MN, Champlin MN, Chicago IL, Commerce CA or Mid-Atlantic sites - no Forgent-specific review corpus exists yet; the company was founded in 2023

Open-role counts on forgentpower.com/careers and /open-positions - the listing table renders client-side and no job count, title list or posting date could be extracted, so no read on hiring acceleration or freeze

The 3 Sep 2026 Form 4 cluster (CEO Niederpruem 88,029 RSUs + 214,335 options, CFO Fiedler 2,817 + 6,859, CAO Lund 7,043 + 17,147, all struck $29.27, all dated 1 Sep) - this is the routine annual grant for a 30 June fiscal-year company, all code A, no open-market purchases or sales, so no signal either way
A named customer for the >$100m data-center order or the 12%-of-revenue Q3 customer disclosed in the 10-Q - no counterparty identified anywhere, so no customer-capex cross-check was possible
Any investor-conference appearance, 8-K or press release between 6 Jul and 27 Aug that would carry a backlog or bookings datapoint fresher than the 31 May prospectus number - there is none
A registration statement filed after 29 Jun 2026 that would signal an imminent fourth Neos deal - EDGAR shows no S-1 or S-3 since, and the company is not S-3 eligible until Feb 2027
Covenant or liquidity stress - the $600m term loan was repriced 26 May, the $250m revolver is undrawn, and the 7.50x first-lien covenant only springs above 40% revolver utilisation
Product recalls, plant incidents, customer complaint threads or distributor/contractor forum chatter about Forgent lead times or quality
baseline_tension: My net is mildly positive and that CUTS AGAINST the run-up (-26.7% over 20 days, 3.9% off the 52-week low, and roughly -9% on the session the baseline was sealed as GLJ's sell initiation on GE Vernova took the whole AI-power complex down) but AGREES with the skew (-22.46 vol points, calls bid, put/call OI 0.30), which is why I kept the number small - the options market is already paying for the bounce, so most of what I found is fighting for the residual rather than adding to a one-sided book.
